What if an existing vacuum deaerator could deliver higher capacity without vacuum systems or oxygen scavenger? 🔧

That question resonated at Tekna Produced Water Management Conference 2026, where Ole Morten Isdahl, CTO at Moreld Minox, presented recent work on a low-height seawater dissolved oxygen stripping concept for offshore water injection.

Traditional vacuum deaeration systems are well proven, but they are often large, height-driven designs and frequently constrained by vacuum pump availability and maintenance. The presentation explored how a compact, positive-pressure approach can remove the vacuum system entirely, reduce overall height and complexity, and still achieve very low dissolved oxygen levels (<20 ppb) without oxygen scavenger.

For existing installations, this opens the possibility to upgrade vacuum towers to higher capacity and improved uptime.
Case studies indicate that such upgrades can enable capacity increases in the range of ~40–100%, depending on system configuration and operating conditions, while lowering operating cost and simplifying offshore operation.

The concept builds on field-proven elements already in operation, including Minox fuel gas deaerator revamps, an eductor-based upgrade currently in service, and the traditional Minox tower solution with multiple offshore installations. Combined with recent testing at the Minox Test Center in Notodden, this provides a strong technical foundation for further deployment.

Et tregjerde trenger jevnlig vask og behandling for å tåle klimaet i Oslo-regionen. Fukt, snø, frost og forurensning sliter på treverket gjennom hele året, spesielt i bynære områder hvor vær og luftforurensning påvirker overflaten. Riktig vedlikehold av tregjerde er derfor avgjørende for å sikre lang levetid og et pent uttrykk rundt boligen.
Hos Grorud Gjerde anbefaler vi regelmessig vedlikehold av gjerde for å forlenge levetiden og redusere behovet for større reparasjoner. Før du beiser eller maler et gjerde, må gjerdet vaskes grundig. Bruk husvask eller et egnet vaskemiddel for utendørs treverk, påfør med kost eller med lavt trykk, og skyll godt etterpå. Det er viktig at treverket får tørke i 1–2 døgn før videre behandling. Dette gjelder enten du har tregjerde i Oslo, hagegjerde i Bærum eller gjerde rundt bolig i Lillestrøm. Getting the analog regulation right is what makes dynamic mobility regulation possible.

There's a paradox in how cities regulate shared mobility: the more dynamic and data-driven the day-to-day regulation needs to be, the more carefully the analog rules — the bylaws, the permit conditions, the procurement documents — need to be drafted.

Bergen's proposed new bylaw gets this balance right. The text sets specific numbers and times, but every parameter comes with explicit language about how it can be adjusted without going through another lengthy bylaw revision. 

Vehicle caps per zone. Night closures. Service availability windows. Operator counts. 

All adjustable within the regulatory framework once the bylaw is in place.

That's not a small thing. In too many cities, the bylaw locks in a 2022 understanding of micromobility and then becomes the bottleneck when the market, the technology, or the city's needs change in 2026. 

Operators consolidate. E-bikes enter the mix. New use cases emerge around transit integration. 

The bylaw, written for a different reality, becomes the obstacle.

Three design choices stand out in Bergen's draft:

→ Permits are tied to a service concession contract, integrating the future bike-share scheme into the same regulatory regime as e-scooters. One framework, not two parallel ones.

→ Different vehicle types can be regulated differently. E-bikes and e-scooters have different footprints, different use cases, different safety profiles. Treating them identically was always a workaround.

→ Vehicle caps can now be applied to small areas within zones, not just whole zones. A targeted tool for targeted problems, instead of blunt city-wide adjustments.

In the Nivel consultation response, we highlighted the need to having the ability to sort out things on a local/micro level – where the challenges are – and employing fees as a dynamic management measure. 

The dynamic part — geofences, real-time data, automated compliance — only works if the analog foundation gives the city room to use those tools. Bergen kommune has been a frontrunner on the operational side since 2020. The new bylaw makes sure the legal foundation keeps up.
